 Falcons look to rebound against Bulls in Buffalo
 Carter Leonard , Falcon Media Sports Network 
 October 23, 2026 
 BOWLING GREEN, OH – OCTOBER 17: Bowling Green Falcons junior quarterback Jay Kastantin #17 throws a short pass to graduate tight end Blane Cleaver #89 during a Mid-American Conference football game between the Ball State Cardinals and the Bowling Green Falcons at Doyt L. Perry Stadium in Bowling Green, Ohio. (Coyle Withrow/BG Falcon Media) 
 The Bowling Green Falcons (2-5, 2-1) are heading east to Buffalo, New York for their first of a two road game stretch against the Buffalo Bulls (4-3, 2-1) at UB Stadium on Saturday, Oct 24. at 3:30 p.m.   
 Matchup History   
 Bowling Green leads the series all-time, 13-9. Their first meeting dates back on Sept. 23, 2000, when the Bulls emerged victorious, 20-17. Bowling Green then went on to win 11 out of the next 14 matchups in that time span. However, BG has only won two out of the last seven games. Coincidentally, both wins were on the road.    
 The Bulls, led by head coach Pete Lembo , dominated in last year’s matchup at Doyt L. Perry Stadium, 28-3.   
 The Lowdown   
 Head coach Eddie George and company look to rebound in the MAC standings after a 32-31 overtime loss against the Ball State Cardinals at home. Containing the rushing was the struggle for the Orange and Brown allowing 240 rushing yards. 125 of which came from junior quarterback Keldric Luster. George acknowledges that stopping the run, especially a team like the Bulls, is priority number one on the list.   
 “We’re going to have to establish some of that defensively and clog the holes for what they like to do,” George said in his weekly press conference. “From a run game standpoint, they are efficient in running the football.”   
 For the Falcons, the ground game was less than stellar. Only 98 yards rushing amongst six different players. Finding the balance that coach George has been looking for in this offense continues to be a conundrum.   
 “We’re going to have to establish the run, it’s what we’re going to have to do,” George said. “We’ll have to throw it when we need to, and put a game plan together that puts us in the best position to get effective runs, look at some of the stuff they did to us last year, and put a plan together that allows us to be balanced offensively.”   
 This season for Lembo and the Bulls has seen a steady rise towards the top along with the MAC’s elite. Coming off back-to-back wins against the Toledo Rockets, 23-8, and Massachusetts Minutemen, 25-18 in overtime.   
 The rushing attack is the strong suit with senior running back Messiah Burch leading the conference with 118 attempts for 661 yards, averaging 5.6 yards a carry, and scored two touchdowns. Burch has also rushed for 100 yards in four straight games, becoming the first tailback to accomplish such a stat for UB since Jaret Patterson in 2019.   
 Inconsistency is plaguing the passing game as sophomore quarterback Jason Wright ranks second-to-last in average passing yards at 143.3, six touchdowns and four interceptions to add on.  BG’s defense will look to apply pressure to Wright, as well as beginning a new sack streak after they were unsuccessful in getting to Luster the previous week.   
 Falcon Four Players To Watch:   
 Falcons, RB: Nakai Amachree : Establishing the run game is the motto for BG. The plan could include more Amachree in the backfield if sophomore Austyn Dendy is unable to get off to a fast start. The Haslett, Michigan native is also known for his speed, showcasing it in his 64-yard touchdown reception in week four against Miami (OH).   
 Falcons, Safety: D’Kyah Banks : Banks has done more than back-to-back fumble recovery touchdowns in two straight games. 12 tackles across the last two games and flying from sideline to sideline could disrupt the Bulls offensive flow.     
 Bulls, TE: Clint Walker :  The receiving game for the Bulls has seen a mix of names come up strong, the same could be said for Walker with two trips to the endzone in last week’s victory. Walker averaged 6.4 yards a reception, the pass catching ability and physicality could bode well against a Falcons secondary that gives up big chunk plays down field.   
 Bulls , RB: Messiah Burch : Lembo will continue to feed the hot hand of Burch. The senior is coming off a 28 carries, 172 yard performance against UMass and will look to cause havoc against the front four of Bowling Green.   
 Falcon Media Sports Network will travel along with a broadcast from Holden Ruck and Sam Bork on Falcon Radio, with a recap of the game from Kevin Hutchinson on bgfalconmedia.com .
